comment: The applications the weekly run reads, and why these.
How the list was built (2026-09-22, re-checkable): the 300 most-starred non-archived PHP
repositories on GitHub, plus a hand list of applications whose deployment base is larger
than their star count — 109 repositories looked at in all. Each was asked one question
first: is there a composer.lock at all? Then, for those that have one: what is the newest
stable release, and does that release carry composer.json and composer.lock? 61 came
through. This list is chosen from those 61 on two signals and one constraint.
Signal one, installed base, for the tier where it is measured by someone else: W3Techs,
2026-09-21 — Joomla 1.1% of all websites, Drupal 0.6%, Adobe (Magento) 0.6%. WordPress is
40.2% and is not here: its core repository ships no composer.lock, so there is nothing to
read. Signal two, attention: GitHub stars, which is what puts Coolify (62k), Appwrite
(57k) and Bagisto (28k) at the top of any list of PHP applications today.
The constraint is the release. A project that does not commit a lock file at a tagged
release cannot be read this way at all, and that rules out a surprising number of large
ones: Shopware, Sylius, Pimcore, Dolibarr, Roundcube, osTicket, Piwigo, SilverStripe,
Contao, Statamic, October, MODX, ProcessWire, Vanilla and YetiForce ship no lock in the
repository, and Nextcloud's has no production packages in it (they are vendored
separately). That is a fact about the ecosystem, not a gap in this list.
Near misses, if the list grows: humhub/humhub, glpi-project/glpi, concretecms/concretecms,
chamilo/chamilo-lms, librenms/librenms, kimai/kimai, espocrm/espocrm, SuiteCRM/SuiteCRM,
koel/koel, pixelfed/pixelfed, getgrav/grav, dokuwiki/dokuwiki (tag_pattern
^release-\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}[a-z]?$), openemr/openemr (^v\d+(_\d+)*$). Adding one costs a
job and a few hundred GitHub API calls a week; the ceiling that bites first is the
token's, not the runner's.
Fields: `lock` is the path inside the repository, which is not always the root.
`tag_pattern` overrides the default stable-version match for a project that does not tag
with version numbers (phpBB's `release-3.3.17`, phpMyAdmin's `RELEASE_5_2_3`); see
scripts/watch_plan.py. `target_php` is 8.4 for every project, as the post used: it decides
the old-promise verdict only, and a number chosen per project would make that column mean
a different thing in every row.
starters_comment: The other half of the run: not what a project ships, but what `composer create-project`
gives someone starting one today. Two reasons this is a table of its own.
One, it is the only way most of the ecosystem can be measured at all. Shopware, Sylius,
TYPO3's distribution, Craft, Statamic, Pimcore and WordPress-through-Bedrock commit no
lock file to their repository; their dependency tree exists only once someone installs
them. Two, a fresh install is a genuinely different question — its tree is whatever the
current constraints resolve to this week, with no history to blame — and the answer is not
always clean: a `composer create-project pimcore/skeleton` on 2026-09-22 printed
'Package pimcore/quill-bundle is abandoned' before lockrot had said anything at all.
Each entry is resolved, never installed: `composer create-project --no-install
--no-scripts --no-plugins`, then `composer update --no-install`, so a lock file is written
and not one line of a third party's code is executed. The starter package is pinned to its
newest stable version on Packagist so the row names something checkable; everything under
it resolves fresh, which is the point. `require` is what follows the create, for the
variants that are a create plus a package — `symfony new --webapp` is Symfony's skeleton
plus symfony/webapp-pack, and the bare skeleton alone is one package, which is a fact
worth showing next to it.
Names are prefixed `new-` because a starter and a release can be the same project (TYPO3
is both), and both write a report into the same directory.
Verified on 2026-09-22: every entry below resolves to a lock file under those flags.
Also tried and working, if the list grows: laminas/laminas-mvc-skeleton.
